story.headline: CARDINALS AND REDS STAGE DOUBLEHEADER DRAMA IN CINCINNATI, SPLITTING A WILD PAIR
story.deck: Walker homers twice across two games as Reds survive 11 innings in the nightcap
story.body:
CINCINNATI — Christian Walker had himself a day for the ages at Great American Ball Park on Saturday, clubbing home runs in both ends of a doubleheader as the St. Louis Cardinals and Cincinnati Reds split a wild twin bill, with St. Louis taking the opener 8-1 before the Reds edged the Cardinals 7-6 in 11 innings in the nightcap before a crowd of 31,144.

In the opener, Walker launched his 14th home run of the year as part of a Cardinals attack that also featured solo shots from Torres and Nolan Lowe, whose seventh of the season came as part of a two-run seventh inning. St. Louis sent 21 runners to base in the brisk 2-hour, 39-minute contest, scattering runs across the middle and late innings to pull away from Cincinnati, which had briefly led 1-0 after the second before the Cardinals seized control in the third.

The nightcap proved far more punishing. The Reds erupted for five runs in the fifth inning to seize control, only to watch St. Louis answer with three in the sixth. Walker blasted his 15th of the season, Lowe added his eighth, and Felix Fermin and cruise Cruz also went deep as both clubs loaded the bases repeatedly — the Cardinals stranded 23 runners and the Reds 18 through 11 innings. A pinch-hit home run tied the game in the ninth, but Cincinnati reliever Leahy earned the win when the Reds pushed across the walk-off run in the 11th, ending a marathon that consumed 3 hours and 25 minutes.
